import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.39

by B. I. Plotkin

A class of groups $\mathfrak{K}$ is said to be *radical* if it is closed under taking
homomorphic images and normal subgroups and if every group generated by its normal
$\mathfrak{K}$-subgroups also belongs to $\mathfrak{K}$. The question proposed relates to the
topic "Radical classes and formulae of Narrow (first order) Predicate Calculus (NPC)". One can
show that the only non-trivial radical class definable by universal formulae of NPC is the class
of all groups. Recently (in a letter to me), G. M. Bergman constructed a family of locally finite
radical classes definable by formulae of NPC. Do there exist similar classes which are not
locally finite and different from the class of all groups? In particular, does there exist a
radical class of groups which is closed under taking Cartesian products, contains an infinite
cyclic group, and is different from the class of all groups?

Here a class of groups is a predicate on groups (in `Type`); closure under homomorphic images
makes it closed under isomorphism. "Definable by formulae of NPC" is read as: the class is the
class of models of some set of sentences of the first-order language of groups (with symbols
`*`, `⁻¹`, `1`); a class defined by a single sentence is the special case of a singleton set.
A class is *locally finite* if all its groups are locally finite, i.e. all their finitely
generated subgroups are finite. Cartesian products are unrestricted direct products of arbitrary
families.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isLocallyFinite_multiplicative_int : ¬ IsLocallyFinite (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro h
  have : Finite (⊤ : Subgroup (Multiplicative ℤ)) := h ⊤ (Group.fg_def.mp inferInstance)
  have : Finite (Multiplicative ℤ) := Finite.of_equiv _ Subgroup.topEquiv.toEquiv
  exact not_finite (Multiplicative ℤ)

claims.decomposer_note: "Similar classes" = radical classes (isomorphism-closed classes of groups closed under homomorphic images, normal subgroups, and such that a group generated by (= equal to the join of) its normal K-subgroups lies in K) that are definable by first-order formulae in the language of groups (a set of sentences, i.e. an elementary/axiomatizable class, a single sentence being the special case — the statement is ambiguous between the two); "not locally finite" means the class contains at least one group that is not locally finite (which already forces non-triviality); the preceding sentence about universal formulae is an asserted known fact, not a question, so it is not a separate sub-question.
claims.reviewer_why: Faithful: ∃ 𝔎 radical (surjective images, normal subgroups, join of normal 𝔎-subgroups = ⊤ ⟹ member) ∧ axiomatizable by a set of first-order sentences in the bespoke language (·,⁻¹,1) ∧ contains a group with an infinite finitely generated subgroup ∧ omits some group. Lives in universe Type like the other Kourovka files; uses an instance for the language structure and includes a semantic test (abelian groups are definable) that confirms the funMap encoding. Edits: renamed IsRadical → IsRadicalClass (avoids shadowing Mathlib's root IsRadical), docstring note on single-sentence special case, added trivial-group boundary test.

namespace Kourovka.«6.39»

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

/-- A class of groups, i.e. a predicate on groups. -/
abbrev GroupClass := ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop

/-- A class of groups $\mathfrak{K}$ is *radical* if it is closed under taking homomorphic
images and normal subgroups, and every group generated by its normal $\mathfrak{K}$-subgroups
(i.e. equal to the join of its normal subgroups lying in $\mathfrak{K}$) also belongs to
$\mathfrak{K}$. -/
structure IsRadicalClass (𝔎 : GroupClass) : Prop where
  /-- $\mathfrak{K}$ is closed under taking homomorphic images. -/
  of_surjective : ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H] (f : G →* H),
    Function.Surjective f → 𝔎 G → 𝔎 H
  /-- $\mathfrak{K}$ is closed under taking normal subgroups. -/
  of_normal : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (N : Subgroup G), N.Normal → 𝔎 G → 𝔎 N
  /-- A group generated by its normal $\mathfrak{K}$-subgroups belongs to $\mathfrak{K}$. -/
  of_sSup_normal : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ 𝔎 N} = ⊤ → 𝔎 G

/-- A group is *locally finite* if every finitely generated subgroup is finite. -/
def IsLocallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Finite H

/-- The function symbols of the first-order language of groups: multiplication (arity `2`),
inversion (arity `1`) and the identity (arity `0`). -/
inductive GroupFunc : ℕ → Type
  | mul : GroupFunc 2
  | inv : GroupFunc 1
  | one : GroupFunc 0

/-- The first-order language of groups, with function symbols `*`, `⁻¹`, `1` and no relation
symbols. -/
def groupLanguage : Language where
  Functions := GroupFunc
  Relations _ := Empty

/-- Every group is a structure for the first-order language of groups, the symbols being
interpreted by the group operations. -/
instance (G : Type*) [Group G] : groupLanguage.Structure G where
  funMap {n} f :=
    match n, f with
    | _, .mul => fun x => x 0 * x 1
    | _, .inv => fun x => (x 0)⁻¹
    | _, .one => fun _ => 1
  RelMap r := r.elim

/-- A class of groups $\mathfrak{K}$ is *definable by formulae of first-order predicate calculus*
(axiomatizable) if there is a set $T$ of sentences of the first-order language of groups such
that a group belongs to $\mathfrak{K}$ if and only if it satisfies every sentence of $T$. -/
def IsFirstOrderDefinable (𝔎 : GroupClass) : Prop :=
  ∃ T : groupLanguage.Theory, ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝔎 G ↔ G ⊨ T

/--
Does there exist a radical class of groups $\mathfrak{K}$, definable by formulae of first-order
predicate calculus, which is not locally finite (i.e. contains a group that is not locally
finite) and is different from the class of all groups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.39» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ 𝔎 : GroupClass, IsRadicalClass 𝔎 ∧ IsFirstOrderDefinable 𝔎 ∧
      (∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), 𝔎 G ∧ ¬ IsLocallyFinite G) ∧
      (∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), ¬ 𝔎 G) := by
  sorry

/--
Does there exist a radical class of groups $\mathfrak{K}$ which is closed under taking Cartesian
products (unrestricted direct products of arbitrary families), contains an infinite cyclic group,
and is different from the class of all groups?

No first-order definability assumption is imposed in this question.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.39».variants.cartesian_products : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ 𝔎 : GroupClass, IsRadicalClass 𝔎 ∧
      (∀ (ι : Type) (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, Group (G i)], (∀ i, 𝔎 (G i)) → 𝔎 (∀ i, G i)) ∧
      (∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Infinite G ∧ IsCyclic G ∧ 𝔎 G) ∧
      (∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), ¬ 𝔎 G) := by
  sorry

/-- The class of all groups is radical. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isRadicalClass_univ : IsRadicalClass fun _ _ => True :=
  ⟨fun _ _ _ _ _ _ _ => trivial, fun _ _ _ _ _ => trivial, fun _ _ _ => trivial⟩

/-- Every radical class contains the trivial group, which is generated by the empty family of
normal subgroups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsRadicalClass.unit {𝔎 : GroupClass} (h : IsRadicalClass 𝔎) : 𝔎 Unit :=
  h.of_sSup_normal Unit (Subsingleton.elim _ _)

/-- The class of all groups is definable by first-order formulae (by the empty set of
sentences). -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem isFirstOrderDefinable_univ : IsFirstOrderDefinable fun _ _ => True :=
  ⟨∅, fun _ _ => ⟨fun _ => inferInstance, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩

/-- The class of abelian groups is definable by first-order formulae, namely by the sentence
$\forall x\, \forall y,\ x y = y x$. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem isFirstOrderDefinable_comm :
    IsFirstOrderDefinable fun G _ => ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x := by
  refine ⟨{∀' ∀' (Functions.apply₂ (GroupFunc.mul : groupLanguage.Functions 2) (&0) (&1) ='
    Functions.apply₂ (GroupFunc.mul : groupLanguage.Functions 2) (&1) (&0))}, fun G _ => ?_⟩
  simp only [Theory.model_iff, Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, Sentence.Realize,
    Formula.Realize, BoundedFormula.realize_all, BoundedFormula.realize_bdEqual,
    Term.realize_functions_apply₂]
  exact Iff.rfl

/-- The infinite cyclic group is not locally finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isLocallyFinite_multiplicative_int : ¬ IsLocallyFinite (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  intro h
  have : Finite (⊤ : Subgroup (Multiplicative ℤ)) := h ⊤ (Group.fg_def.mp inferInstance)
  have : Finite (Multiplicative ℤ) := Finite.of_equiv _ Subgroup.topEquiv.toEquiv
  exact not_finite (Multiplicative ℤ)

end Kourovka.«6.39»

items: Classes of groups are predicates on groups in universe `Type` (consistent with the other Kourovka files); Cartesian products are over index types ι : Type with factors in Type, so all products stay in Type.
Isomorphism closure is not stated separately: it follows from closure under homomorphic images, which is stated as: for every surjective group hom G →* H, 𝔎 G → 𝔎 H.

'Every group generated by its normal 𝔎-subgroups belongs to 𝔎' is stated as sSup {N : Subgroup G | N.Normal ∧ 𝔎 N} = ⊤ → 𝔎 G. For the trivial group this forces the trivial group into every radical class (sSup ∅ = ⊥ = ⊤); this is standard for radical classes and irrelevant to both questions, whose classes contain a nontrivial group and hence its trivial quotient anyway.

'Definable by formulae of NPC' is read as definable by a SET of first-order sentences (an axiomatizable/elementary class), the more general of the two readings the decomposition notes mention; a single sentence is the special case T = {φ}. The language has symbols (·, ⁻¹, 1); definability does not depend on this choice of standard signature.
'Not locally finite' (for a class) is stated as: the class contains a group that is not locally finite, where a group is locally finite iff every finitely generated subgroup (Subgroup.FG) is finite.
'Contains an infinite cyclic group' is stated literally as ∃ G, Infinite G ∧ IsCyclic G ∧ 𝔎 G rather than as 𝔎 (Multiplicative ℤ); the two are equivalent by isomorphism closure.
'Different from the class of all groups' is stated as ∃ G, ¬ 𝔎 G.
The Cartesian-product variant carries no first-order definability hypothesis, as literally stated and as the decomposition table prescribes.

Four short `@[category test]` theorems with real proofs were added to test the bespoke definitions (the class of all groups is radical and first-order definable; abelian groups are first-order definable via ∀x∀y, xy = yx, which checks the semantics of the structure instance; Multiplicative ℤ is not locally finite), following CONTRIBUTING's request for basic API tests of bespoke definitions.

reviewer_notes: All eight candidates agreed on the mathematical reading; differences were stylistic. Chose the Type-universe, instance-based formulation (c05/c06/c07 family) over universe-polymorphic ones (c02, c04, c08): a universe-polymorphic theorem with a single answer(sorry) Prop is awkward, and Type matches the existing Kourovka files. Verified in a scratch file: isomorphism closure follows from the surjective-image clause; the trivial group is forced into every radical class (sSup ∅ = ⊥ = ⊤), which is faithful to 'generated by its (empty family of) normal 𝔎-subgroups' and irrelevant to both questions; the Structure instance's funMap reduces to x*y, x⁻¹, 1 by rfl. Ambiguity: 'definable by formulae of NPC' is read as axiomatizable by a set of sentences (single sentence = singleton special case), as the decomposition notes allow; this is recorded in the module docstring. Mathlib has Language.ring but no language of groups and no locally-finite-group predicate, so bespoke definitions were necessary; they are kept in the problem file per the single-file constraint (a reviewer may wish to move groupLanguage/IsLocallyFinite to FormalConjecturesForMathlib). Final file compiles with only 'declaration uses sorry' warnings.
statement: A class of groups ${\goth K}$ is said to be radical if it is closed under taking homomorphic images and normal subgroups and if every group generated by its normal ${\goth K} $-subgroups also belongs to ${\goth K}$. The question proposed relates to the topic “Radical classes and formulae of Narrow (first order) Predicate Calculus (NPC)”. One can show that the only non-trivial radical class definable by universal formulae of NPC is the class of all groups. Recently (in a letter to me), G. M. Bergman constructed a family of locally finite radical classes definable by formulae of NPC. Do there exist similar classes which are not locally finite and different from the class of all groups? In particular, does there exist a radical class of groups which is closed under taking Cartesian products, contains an infinite cyclic group, and is different from the class of all groups?
